text:
maria: Heads-up — Dedicated roll 4f3a9c3 is causing a p95 tail spike for a long-seq workload on customer X. Observed during canary. Holding the rollout.
aj: saw it in the alert stream too, p95 jumped from ~85ms -> ~140ms on a few pods.
trent: what changed in 4f3a9c3? I thought it was just an autobatch tuning tweak.
maria: it landed an autobatch heuristic change + a kernel-hinting optimization that tries to prefer small-kernel paths for short prefixes. Seems to be thrashing on mixed-length requests.
sera: CI perf job flagged this earlier: runtime-integration-perf failed on p95 by +12% but it was marked flaky and merged.
ci-bot: [runtime-integration-perf] Job failed: p95 latency regression (+12%). Link: https://ci.redwood/runtime/12345
aj: ugh, flaky suppression bit us. Does the perf regression reproduce locally?
lucy: I repro'd against a dedicated canary pool with traffic replay. Quick prof run shows kernel switches spiking and KV prefetch misses up.
trent: paste the profiler snippet? even a tiny one helps.
lucy: ```
merge: 4f3a9c3
baseline p95: 82ms
canary p95: 137ms
kernel_switches/sec: 78 -> 910
kv_fetch_misses/sec: 1200 -> 4200
avg tokens/sec per worker: 320 -> 290
``` 
maria: that kernel_switches/sec number is the smoking gun — the runtime keeps flipping kernels between small/large inference paths which prevents cache-friendly execution.
aj: sounds like the kernel-hinting heuristic is over-eager. For dedicated capacity we need stability > micro-optimizations that oscillate.
trent: we should decide revert vs feature-flag rollback. Revert is fast but noisy. We have an opt-out flag for the new heuristic right?
lucy: yes, config flag `enable_autobatch_hint_v2=false` in rollout config. Can toggle per-pool.
sera: plan: 1) hold rollout (done), 2) flip flag for affected pools to false, 3) run canary replay for 30m, 4) if stable, continue rollout without hint v2, 5) CI follow-up and bisect. Agree?
aj: +1. Also need a hotpatch to the canary probes so they stress long-seq customers specifically.
maria: I've opened a hotpatch PR to flip the flag in the canary group and add a targeted probe: https://git.redwood/p/runtime/merge/4321
ci-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary update queued to pool dedicated-canary-3
oncall-bot: Incident: SLA risk flagged for customer X; paging oncall list. Severity: P2.
trent: I'll schedule a quick rollback if the flag flip doesn't help within 20 minutes.
lucy: after flipping the flag we should watch KV miss rate and kernel_switches/sec.
aj: what about customer impact window — did any requests time out or just slower p95?
maria: no timeouts, just p95 and tail latencies. Customers reported slower interactive responses but nothing critical yet. Still SLA risk if sustained.
sera: CI action item: remove flaky suppression on runtime-integration-perf and add a targeted long-seq workload.
trent: I'll take the CI change after we stabilise the rollout.
maria: action owners: maria -> hold and coordinate customer comms, lucy -> deploy flag hotpatch and monitor, aj -> run replay traces and collect profiler snapshots, trent -> CI follow-up and rollback readiness, sera -> create perf regression issue and re-enable CI gate.
lucy: flag hotpatch applied to dedicated-canary-3. Monitoring now.
aj: running a 15m heavyseq replay now. Will paste tail histograms when done.
lucy: early numbers look good: kernel_switches/sec down to ~110, kv_fetch_misses/sec down to ~1300, p95 trending back to ~90ms.
maria: great. keep monitoring for 1 hour then decide resume rollout.
trent: note for postmortem: avoid merging perf-flaky PRs without gating and add canary probes that include mixing short/long sequences.
maria: agreed. I'll open the postmortem ticket and add the action items.
aj: thanks everyone. ping if anything changes. :thumbsup:
